audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer chart was a blanket Skill on all seven rows while content win[] and the packet read [Viktor x4, Skill, Skill, Viktor]. Eighteen fields also misgender Anivia as he/him.
audit.why: Anivia is mana-starved and immobile pre-6 while Viktor's E shoves and pokes for free; Glacial Storm plus Rebirth even it from 6 through first item; two items out-range her storm. Content whys already argue this.
audit.corrected: Sides on rows 0-3 and 6 moved to Viktor with rewritten whys and ratings; rows 4-5 stay Skill with whys de-templated; win[] untouched per the chart rule.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Death Ray' fabricated in spikes[0].text and content early; kit names Viktor's E Hextech Ray.
audit.corrected: Renamed in both places. Spike set (pre-6 mana bully / R+egg stabilization / first-item perma-clear / late out-range) is sound.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digits; two bullets were verbatim tradeGood/tradeBad bleed; both missingInteractions (Flash Frost cancels Arcane Storm's channel; Crystallize cuts retreat and Viktor has no dash) were absent.
audit.why: Flash Frost is 11s at rank 1 and a projectile stun — any CC cancels Viktor's R channel per his kit flag. Frostbite is 4s and doubles after a Q hit. Crystallize is a 17s-cooldown terrain wall; Viktor is dashless so it converts a chase into a Flash check.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns rewritten with numbers; bleed bullets replaced with the channel-cancel rule and the wall-cuts-retreat warning.

audit.why: 11s at rank 1 defines the safe trade window after a sidestep.

edits.before: You dominate the early levels because Anivia is brutally mana-hungry and completely immobile, while your E (Death Ray) lets you shove and poke her off the wave for free. Push the first waves in and force her to either miss CS under tower or burn mana she can't afford. Her Q (Flash Frost) is slow and telegraphed, so sidestep it and she has no way to trade back. Build a CS and health lead before her defensive spike arrives.
